title: Towards generalisable hate speech detection: a review on obstacles and solutions

bias_targets.methodology: Reviewing studies that compare model predictions and false positive rates on African-American English versus white-aligned English tweets, as well as predicting author race demographics from user profiles.
Summarizing approaches that evaluate models using synthetic test sets balanced with gender identity terms, and predicting author gender demographics from user profiles.
Analyzing model tendencies to produce false positives when encountering neutral sexual orientation identity terms (e.g., 'gay') using synthetic test sets.
Referencing studies that predict author age from user profile pictures using computer vision APIs to evaluate demographic disparities.
Examining studies that evaluate intersectional biases in hate speech datasets across user party identification.

Evaluating datasets for non-random sampling artifacts by calculating Pointwise Mutual Information (PMI) for topic-specific words (e.g., sports) and analyzing the overrepresentation of specific prolific users.
